class_id: a container is unwrapped to one member, and the other members are silently dropped
feature: any download that arrives as an archive or bundle (zip, multi-attachment mail, multi-file API response) where the reader picks ONE member to keep
symptom: a bundle is treated as a wrapper around one file, so the unwrap step chooses a member (by name, else the largest) and discards the rest without a trace. When the bundle actually carries several distinct documents, every member except the chosen one is lost, and anything the lost members would have changed never happens. Nothing fails: the chosen member is valid, the store has a row, and the missing documents are absent rows, which no per-row check can see. Universal shape: an unwrap step that returns one thing from a container of N answers a narrower question (which member is the one we wanted?) than the one the data poses (what did the container hold?).

fix_prs: item 22 zip-members PR #969 (branch feat/item22-zip-members). Round 1-2: the unwrap reports every PDF member; each non-GID member typed as a type other than the main document's is stored as its own document row keyed by a STABLE member identity, url '<zip>#member=<url-encoded member path>' (never by position: HTEL's RHP is part 5, so a reorder would swap bytes), part_number = its zip position; a member whose sha256 is already stored for the IPO in any run (DB lookup, OD-33) writes no row; each type a member supplies is marked FOUND in document_fetch_state so its fallback chain stops, ONLY when every consulted exchange answered (round 2 MAJOR 1, round 3 MAJOR 1: an exchange that could not be read must never let an older zip copy close a type the exchange might still supply a newer link for). Round 3: a stored zip whose members were never examined (pre-fix rows) is expanded by the SAME code path, in the pipeline (a bounded per-wake data-slot pass, `stored-zip-expansion-pass.ts`) and by the repair CLI (`scraper/scripts/repair-zip-member-documents.ts`, dry run default, `--expect-db`, `--apply`, ledger); the durable marker `documents.zip_members_checked_at` (migration 0055) records that a zip was examined so it is fetched once. Round 4 (Tier A MAJOR, this class's own recurrence): round 3 marked a zip checked ONLY on HTTP 200, so a permanently dead zip (404, timeout, refused) was left unmarked forever and re-downloaded every wake, and the selection was ordered by `uploaded_at`, so that one dead zip sorted first on every wake and starved the rest of the backlog behind it. Fixed by counting failed re-fetch attempts per zip, once per DISTINCT data slot (`documents.zip_expand_attempts`, `zip_last_attempt_slot`; `DocumentRepository.markZipExpandAttemptFailed`); after 3 distinct-slot failures the zip is marked checked with `documents.zip_unresolved_reason = 'zip_unreachable'` (closed, distinguishable from an expanded zip); the selection is now ordered by last-attempt (`zip_last_attempt_slot ASC NULLS FIRST`), never `uploaded_at`, so a zip that just failed rotates to the back instead of blocking the rest of the backlog.
